bayesmaDatR: Data Management for Bayesian Meta-Analysis

An interactive workbook manager and data-preparation toolkit for Bayesian meta-analysis. Start with the Excel file you already use, organise study and outcome data, then prepare arm-level or two-stage data for modelling.

Overview

bayesmaDatR is designed around an upload → manage → prepare → export workflow. Use the Shiny app to work with an Excel workbook, or use the same data structures from an R script for a reproducible analysis pipeline.

Key features

  • Excel-first workflow: upload, edit, validate, and download a workbook.
  • Outcome-specific data: keep each outcome’s sample sizes, time point, summary statistics, and trial-design correlations with that outcome.
  • Multiple trial designs: record RCT, crossover RCT, cluster RCT, and cluster-crossover RCT data.
  • Flexible summaries: retain means and SDs, medians and quantiles, ranges, event counts, and person-time.
  • Model-ready formats: prepare arm-level data for one-stage, multivariate, multiarm, or longitudinal models, or calculate two-stage yi and sei.
  • Bias assessments: manage the supported robbR tools and INSPECT-SR assessments in the same workbook.

Interactive workflow 

library(bayesmaDatR)

launch_data_entry()

The workbook can contain four sheets: studies, outcomes, risk_of_bias, and inspect_sr. The original app’s sheet names study_details, outcome_data, and rob_data are also recognized. Start with template_ma_data() to see the recommended columns:

template <- template_ma_data()
write_ma_workbook(template, "bayesmaDatR_template.xlsx")

R workflow 

dat <- read_ma_workbook("review.xlsx")
validate_ma_data(dat)

# Two-stage data: one row per study/outcome with yi and sei
es_dat <- as_bayesma(
  dat,
  outcome = "pain_24h",
  model_type = "two_stage",
  measure = "MD"
)

# Arm-level data for one-stage or multivariate models
arm_dat <- as_bayesma(
  dat,
  outcome = "pain_24h",
  model_type = "one_stage"
)

Supported two-stage measures include odds ratios (OR), risk ratios (RR), incidence-rate ratios (IRR), mean differences (MD), standardized mean differences (SMD), and differences in medians (MedD). For median-reported outcomes, convert_median_to_mean() can estimate means and SDs using the Wan or quantile-estimation (qe) method. These calculations use the optional metamedian package.

Risk of bias and INSPECT-SR

Risk-of-bias records identify both the tool and assessment level. Use rob_level = "study" for an assessment applied across a study’s outcomes, or rob_level = "outcome" when a rating applies to one outcome; outcome-level records require an outcome_id.

The INSPECT-SR sheet includes the 21 assessment items and the auxiliary values used for the Carlisle, participant-number consistency, GRIM, and p-value checks. inspect_sr_columns() lists the fields and inspect_sr_labels() gives their display labels. INSPECT-SR judgements are recorded by the reviewer; the package does not infer an overall judgement from the auxiliary calculations.

Package status

bayesmaDatR is under active development. The workbook, validation, and data preparation functions are being expanded alongside package-specific exporters. The current as_bayesma() interface prepares the common data frame; verify model-specific requirements before fitting an analysis.
